title: Advancements in stress-testing methodologies for financial stability applications
summary: This is an ECB Occasional Paper Series publication (No 348) providing a comprehensive overview of stress-testing methodologies developed by the ECB's Financial Stability Committee Working Group on Stress Testing (WGST) from 2018-2022. The paper covers top-down credit risk models, macroprudential stress-testing frameworks including the BEAST model, and system-wide models capturing bank and non-bank interconnectedness. Includes 16 new models developed, 13 new datasets integrated, and expanded focus on climate and cyber risks.
key_points: The WGST developed 16 new stress-testing models between 2018-2022, with 11 covering areas not previously in the ECB top-down toolkit
Five existing models in the STAMP€ tool were replaced or significantly improved
The WGST integrated 13 new datasets including transaction-level data
Models cover credit risk (IFRS 9 and regulatory parameters), market risk, and profitability
The BEAST model is highlighted as the macroprudential stress-testing workhorse model
New focus areas include climate risk and cyber risk assessment
why_it_matters: This paper documents ECB internal supervisory methodology for stress-testing European banks. While not a market-moving publication, it provides insight into how the ECB assesses systemic risk and bank solvency under adverse scenarios—relevant for understanding prudential policy direction and potential regulatory impacts on European banks.
macro_context: Published by ECB Financial Stability Committee Working Group on Stress Testing (WGST) as part of Occasional Paper Series. Covers the 2018-2022 period of stress-testing methodology development, including COVID-19 pandemic stress testing applications and climate risk assessment expansion.
market_structure_context: While the paper focuses on prudential stress-testing rather than market structure in the trading/microstructure sense, system-wide models examining bank and non-bank interconnectedness (ISA model) touch on financial system contagion dynamics relevant to market structure analysis.
